items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: Then the next day she would go visiting, say, 'Hello, there, Frank,' and hit him on his buttocks, and finally she would hit the right one and they'd jump.

ctx.x: No, the only time I would hear him play would be on Sundays. But they all tried to run my mother off the farm, because my father was never home. He was a rounder, you know? And when he was away, his brothers would come up to the house and try to steal the horses, to ride into town at night and different things, you know, and go different places. 'Cause they couldn't take any of my grandfather's horses, you know. And in his absence, they'd come up and steal chickens and my mother would stand there in the door and…

Then the next day she would go visiting, say, 'Hello, there, Frank,' and hit him on his buttocks, and finally she would hit the right one and they'd jump. 'What you running up there, stealing my so-and-so-and-so-and-so.' You know.
How far out of Haskell was the farm?
